knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral Expression For the Arc Length of a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x={t}^{3}-8,\,y={t}^{4}+5t$
from $t=4$ to $t=6$ ?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-8)=3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}+5t)=4{t}^{3}+5\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{6}\sqrt{{(3{t}^{2})}^{2}+{(4{t}^{3}+5)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{6}\sqrt{9{t}^{4}+16{t}^{6}+40{t}^{3}+25}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{6}\sqrt{16{t}^{6}+9{t}^{4}+40{t}^{3}+25}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x={t}^{3}-1,\,y={t}^{2}-t$
from $t=-6$ to $t=-3$ ?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-1)=3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t)=2t-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-6}^{-3}\sqrt{(3{t}^{2})^{2}+(2t-1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-6}^{-3}\sqrt{9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}-4t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x={t}^{3}+{t}^{2},\,y={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}$
from $t=2$ to $t=5$ ?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+{t}^{2})=3{t}^{2}+2t\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})=3{t}^{2}-2t\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{5}\sqrt{{(3{t}^{2}+2t)}^{2}+{(3{t}^{2}-2t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{5}\sqrt{9{t}^{4}+12{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}+9{t}^{4}-12{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{5}\sqrt{18{t}^{4}+8{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{5}t\sqrt{18{t}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x=t-1,\,y={t}^{2}+2$
from $t=7$ to $t=8$ ?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)=1\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+2)=2t\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{7}^{8}\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(2t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{7}^{8}\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x=3{t}^{3}+5,\,y={t}^{2}-5t$
from $t=7$ to $t=9$ ?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{3}+5)=9{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-5t)=2t-5.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{7}^{9}\sqrt{(9{t}^{2})^{2}+(2t-5)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{7}^{9}\sqrt{81{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}-20t+25}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
